title: Topic 7 - Filters & Text Processing
notes: Filters concept: programs that transform input to output in pipelines.
grep basics: grep pattern file; prints lines matching regex.
Extended regex with egrep or grep -E: +, ?, |, {n,m}.
sed basics: stream editor; s/pattern/repl/; global flag g; d deletes lines.
sed examples: sed -e 's/foo/bar/g' file; sed -e '/^$/d' remove blank lines.
awk basics: pattern {action}; fields $1, $2, $0; NR, NF built-ins.
awk example: awk '{print $1,$3}' file; sums: awk '{s+=$1} END {print s}'.
tr basics: character translation; tr A-Z a-z; -d delete; -s squeeze.
sort basics: sort file; -n numeric, -r reverse, -k column, -u unique.
cut basics: cut -b byte-range, cut -f field-range -d delimiter.
paste basics: merge lines of files side by side; paste f1 f2.
Combining filters in pipelines for data processing.
find vs. grep: file discovery vs. content matching.
Examples: grep error logfile | wc -l; cut -d',' -f2 data.csv | sort -u.
Regular expressions cheat sheet for grep/sed/awk.
Best practices: quote regex, test incrementally, prefer awk for structured data.
Performance notes: grep -F faster for fixed strings; LC_ALL=C speeds up sort.
Course relevance: essential for labs, log parsing, automation.
Outside class: used in scripting, pipelines, and DevOps tooling.
